syntax.guarded_form: @p mov.b32 d, a;  (alternatively @!p mov.b32 d, a;)
syntax.source_syntax_quote:
mov.type  d, a;
mov.type  d, sreg;
mov.type  d, avar;       // get address of variable
mov.type  d, avar+imm;   // get address of variable with offset
mov.u32   d, fname;      // get address of device function
mov.u64   d, fname;      // get address of device function
mov.u32   d, kernel;     // get address of entry function
mov.u64   d, kernel;     // get address of entry function

.type = { .pred,
          .b16, .b32, .b64,
          .u16, .u32, .u64,
          .s16, .s32, .s64,
                .f32, .f64 };
syntax_notes: .b32 is listed in the scalar mov .type set; the bounded base form is the .b32 instantiation of 'mov.type d, a;'.
The other scalar syntax variants (sreg, avar, avar+imm, fname, kernel) are recorded as official source facts but are out of the bounded base scope (AMB-2, PTX-MOV-SEM2-013).

The optional guard predicate is omitted from instruction-description syntax (section 9.7) but may prefix any PTX instruction as @{!}p (section 9.3); the general predication form is defined in section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @), incl. 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-MOV-SEM2-072). The guarded_form spelling lists the two guard spellings; @p and @!p have opposite execution conditions (see guard_semantics) and are not semantically interchangeable.
Section 9.7.9.4 defines a distinct vector pack/unpack mov form with .b32 in its type set; that form is out of the bounded base scope (AMB-1, PTX-MOV-SEM2-052).

roles.d: destination operand. For instructions that create a result value, d is the destination operand (section 9.2); mov writes register d with the value of a (PTX-9.3-MOV-004). The destination is a register variable in the .reg state space for the bounded base form; the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule permits '_' for some instructions, but its applicability to the scalar mov.b32 form is an open question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-047).
roles.a: source operand. For the bounded base form, a is a register variable or an immediate value (PTX-9.3-MOV-002, PTX-9.3-MOV-004). The official scalar mov section also lists sreg, avar, avar+imm, fname, and kernel source categories; those are out of the bounded base scope (PTX-MOV-SEM2-013, AMB-2).

operand_forms_supported_by_evidence: destination register of type .b32 (PTX-9.3-MOV-030 shows .reg .b32 r1, r2; with mov.b32 r1, %tid.x;)
source register (PTX-9.3-MOV-010 shows mov.f32 d,a; for the scalar mov form; no scalar mov.b32 register/immediate example was read, see GAP-4/PTX-MOV-SEM2-040)
source constant immediate (PTX-9.3-MOV-010 shows mov.f32 k,0.1; for the scalar mov form; no .b32 immediate example was read, see GAP-5/PTX-MOV-SEM2-048)
destination bit bucket '_' per the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-9.3-MOV-019); scalar mov.b32 applicability is an open question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-047)
operand_form_evidence_notes: PTX-9.3-MOV-002: 'Set a register variable with the value of a register variable or an immediate value.' establishes register and immediate source categories.
PTX-9.3-MOV-004: 'Write register d with the value of a.' and 'Operand a may be a register, special register, variable with optional offset in an addressable memory space, or function name.'

PTX-9.3-MOV-018: 'For instructions that create a result value, the d operand is the destination operand, while a, b, and c are source operands.' and 'PTX instructions generally have from zero to four operands, plus an optional guard predicate appearing after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode' with form '@p opcode d, a;'.
PTX-9.3-MOV-030: official example 'mov.b32 r1, %tid.x;' where r1 is declared '.reg .b32 r1, r2;' and %tid.x is a special register (sreg source; out of bounded base scope).

types.operand_typing_rule: Operands d and a are typed .b32 or a type compatible with .b32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules (same basic type and same size; signed/unsigned same size; bit-size type compatible with any fundamental type of the same size). The exact formulation of the bit-size compatibility rule for mov.b32 operand typing is an open question (OQ-7; PTX-MOV-SEM2-066).
types.compatibility_rules: Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility. Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type of the same size.
types.notes: mov Notes state that 'only predicate and bit-size types are required' for mov, and that the arithmetic types are included for the programmer's convenience (PTX-9.3-MOV-007).

modifiers.statement: The scalar mov syntax 'mov.type d, a;' has no modifier position in the official syntax block (PTX-9.3-MOV-003). The bounded base mov.b32 form therefore has no modifiers.

static_preconditions.description: Type well-formedness: the instruction type specifier .b32 is a valid bit-size fundamental type of 32-bit width.
Operand typing: operands d and a are type-compatible with instruction type .b32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules.
Destination membership: the destination operand d denotes a declared register variable in the .reg state space, or is the bit bucket '_' (if adopted; applicability open question).
Source form: the source operand a is a register variable or an immediate value.
Guard well-typedness: if a guard is present, it is a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
Version gating: base mov (and therefore the bounded base mov.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.

dynamic_preconditions.description: No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for mov.b32 (for example, no requirement on the values held by source operands, and no flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted.

state_reads.description: When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when a is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.

state_reads.component: guard predicate register p (when a guard is present)
state_reads.description: The value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. The general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 states execution occurs for threads whose guard predicate is True ('Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', PTX-9.3-MOV-035), so the guard read is the predicate value used by that evaluation.

state_writes.component: destination register d (on execution with a real destination register)
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates true and d is a register, the destination register d is updated with the value of source operand a. Only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed: no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status/condition-code component is written by the bounded base mov.b32.

When the destination is the bit bucket '_', the general section 9.2 rule indicates the destination register is replaced by the bit bucket; the represented consequence is that no value register is written (the result is discarded). This is supported only to the strength of the general rule; scalar mov.b32-specific demonstration is absent (open question).

state_writes.component: state when the complete guard expression evaluates false
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and no state component changes. This is now a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION grounded in the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035) with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036), applied to mov.b32 through the general rules that all PTX instructions may be predicated (PTX-9.3-MOV-016) and that all instructions have an optional guard predicate prefix @{!}p (PTX-9.3-MOV-021). Formerly ASSUMPTION in semantics-v1 (PTX-MOV-SEM1-034/038); reclassified after the v2 source-bundle supplement resolved bundle GAP-1 at the source level.

guard_semantics.guard_expression_representation: An optional guard prefix @{!}p appears after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode, where p is a predicate register variable of type .pred, optionally negated with '!'. No guard is present in the syntax-description form (the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax), but all PTX instructions may be predicated. The general predication form is defined in section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @): '@{!}p instruction;' with Description 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035) and Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036).

guard_expression_evaluation.no_guard: The complete guard expression is true; the instruction is executed unconditionally.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_p: @p: the complete guard expression is the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is true.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_bang_p: @!p: the complete guard expression is the logical negation of the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is false. The official example '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over' (PTX-9.3-MOV-022) and the general predication example '@!p div.f32 ratio,x,y // avoid division by zero' (PTX-9.3-MOV-037) show the negated guard executing when the underlying predicate is false.
guard_expression_evaluation.execution_condition: Execution occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true (general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction', PTX-9.3-MOV-036; section 9.3 'controls conditional execution', PTX-9.3-MOV-021). The underlying predicate value is not confused with the evaluated guard expression: for @!p, the guard expression is true exactly when the predicate value is false.

guard_semantics.guard_false_consequence: The represented consequence when the complete guard expression evaluates false is that the instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged. This is now a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038) grounded in the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2: 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035), with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036), applied to mov.b32 through 'All PTX instructions may be predicated' (PTX-9.3-MOV-016) and 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate' (PTX-9.3-MOV-021). Formerly an ASSUMPTION pending human approval in semantics-v1 (bundle GAP-1); the v2 source-bundle supplement resolved GAP-1 at the source level and this stage reclassified the mov.b32 consequence accordingly. The official do-nothing clause is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-MOV-SEM2-072); the state-level reading 'no state component changes' is the semantic interpretation of 'do nothing' and is recorded as DERIVED.
guard_semantics.predication_exception: st.param and ld.param instructions used for argument passing cannot be predicated; this exception does not mention mov and therefore does not restrict mov.b32 predication (PTX-9.3-MOV-032).

behavior.semantic_pseudocode_source: PTX-9.3-MOV-006 (first line of the official mov Semantics block; the remaining lines d = sreg; d = &avar; d = &avar+imm; concern out-of-scope source categories)
behavior.copy_rule: The value written to the destination register d equals the value of source operand a: a bit-for-bit copy of the 32-bit untyped .b32 value. This is derived from 'Write register d with the value of a.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-004), the Semantics line 'd = a;' (PTX-9.3-MOV-006), and the .b32 'Bits (untyped)' 32-bit type (PTX-9.3-MOV-024, PTX-9.3-MOV-026).
behavior.copy_rule_classification: DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-MOV-SEM2-036); the Semantics line itself is SOURCE_FACT (PTX-MOV-SEM2-035).
behavior.guard_true_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction value of source operand a is read (register value or constant immediate), and the destination register d is updated with that value; if d is the bit bucket '_', no register is written (per the general rule, applicability open). Guard-true execution is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036).
behavior.guard_false_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged; this is now a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038) grounded in the explicit official clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035) and its Semantics (PTX-9.3-MOV-036), applied to mov.b32 via the general predicability rules (PTX-9.3-MOV-016, PTX-9.3-MOV-021).
behavior.aliasing_read_before_write: Because the semantics is a value copy (d = a;), the value of a is read before the destination update; if d and a denote the same register, the register retains its own value (read-before-write makes the copy self-consistent). No official scalar mov example with d == a was read (related to GAP-4); this is a derived interpretation at the strength of the copy rule.
behavior.determinism_note: Determinism is not explicitly stated in the source (bundle GAP-2); the execution relation for mov.b32 is derived to be deterministic because the value written is fully determined by the value read (a pure copy with no arithmetic or truncation) and the guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value. See determinism section and PTX-MOV-SEM2-039.

exceptional_behavior.statement: No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 17 status NOT_FOUND; GAP-3). This absence is not asserted as a positive source fact that no exceptional behavior exists; no error, trap, or exceptional behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is recorded as an open question.

undefined_behavior.statement: No explicit undefined-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence (GAP-3). No undefined-behavior claim is made; no undefined behavior is invented.

implementation_defined_behavior.statement: No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made; no implementation-defined behavior is invented.

determinism.statement: The execution relation for mov.b32 is deterministic: for any well-formed state and well-typed mov.b32 instruction, the fully-specified rules determine at most one resulting state. The guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value; the value written is exactly the value read (a pure .b32 bit copy, no arithmetic, no truncation); and the only state write on execution is the destination update. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (bundle gap GAP-2; architecture assumption A-3); it is a derived interpretation stated as proof obligation PRF-1, and it does not depend on any arithmetic-result assumption because mov performs no arithmetic.

version_restrictions.base_mov_b32_introduced_in: PTX ISA version 1.0 (derived: the PTX ISA Notes state 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.' for scalar mov, and mov.b32 is a base scalar mov form).

target_restrictions.base_mov_b32_restriction: No family-specific target restriction is stated for the scalar mov.b32 register/immediate value-copy form in the scalar section read. The Target ISA Notes in section 9.7.9.3 state only 'mov.f64 requires sm_13 or higher.' and 'Taking the address of kernel entry functions requires sm_35 or higher.' (both concerning out-of-scope forms).
target_restrictions.target_set_open_question: The sentence 'Supported on all target architectures.' was read in the vector section 9.7.9.4 (PTX-9.3-MOV-013) and in the general @ predication section 9.7.13.2 (PTX-9.3-MOV-036); both concern forms other than the scalar mov.b32 value-copy base form, so neither establishes the scalar base form's target set without further evidence (bundle GAP-7; architecture assumption A-8). The scalar base form's target set is an open question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-046).

semantic_claims.statement: The construct identity is the mov instruction family: PTX ISA 9.3 section 9.7.9.3 'Data Movement and Conversion Instructions: mov', HTML anchor data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-mov (HTML lines 14999-15002; PDF page 269).
Section 9.1 states that each PTX instruction is described by its name, format, semantics, and examples.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The framing of the mov Syntax/Semantics/Examples blocks as normative source content is an interpretation of the section's role, not part of the quoted text (semantic-critic v1 finding F-1 addressed by moving the interpretive clause here).

semantic_claims.statement: Section 9.7.9 intro states that these instructions copy data from place to place, and that mov, ld, ldu, and st operate on both scalar and vector types.

The bounded unit is the scalar value-copy form 'mov.type d, a;' with instruction type .b32 and source operand a a register variable or an immediate value, per the human-approved architecture bounded-scope decision D-0c (approved at Gate A). The sreg, avar, avar+imm, fname, and kernel source categories and the vector pack/unpack form of section 9.7.9.4 are out of the bounded base scope.

The exact scalar mov syntax variants are 'mov.type d, a;', 'mov.type d, sreg;', 'mov.type d, avar;', 'mov.type d, avar+imm;', 'mov.u32/mov.u64 d, fname;', and 'mov.u32/mov.u64 d, kernel;', with .type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64, .u16, .u32, .u64, .s16, .s32, .s64, .f32, .f64 }. .b32 is in the scalar mov type set; the bounded base form is 'mov.type d, a;'.

Section 9.2 states that PTX instructions generally have from zero to four operands plus an optional guard predicate after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode, with forms including '@p opcode d, a;'; the d, a form matches mov.b32.

The bounded base syntax form is 'mov.b32 d, a;', the .b32 instantiation of 'mov.type d, a;'. The .b32 type specifier is in the scalar mov type set and .b32 is a 32-bit 'Bits (untyped)' fundamental type.
All PTX instructions may be predicated; in the instruction descriptions the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.

All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution; the syntax is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated; instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.

Operand order and role conventions: section 9.2 states 'For instructions that create a result value, the d operand is the destination operand, while a, b, and c are source operands'; the scalar mov syntax lists the destination first as 'mov.type d, a;'.

The mov description is 'Set a register variable with the value of a register variable or an immediate value. Take the non-generic address of a variable in global, local, or shared state space.' The first sentence grounds the register/immediate value-copy behavior of the bounded base form; the address clause concerns the out-of-scope avar form.

The mov execution description is 'Write register d with the value of a.' and 'Operand a may be a register, special register, variable with optional offset in an addressable memory space, or function name.' For the bounded base unit, only the register/immediate categories of a are in scope.

For the bounded base unit, the source operand a is a register variable or an immediate value. The sreg, avar, avar+imm, fname, and kernel source categories are official source facts of section 9.7.9.3 but are out of the bounded base scope (AMB-2); their semantics are not interpreted in this unit.

The official scalar mov Examples block includes 'mov.f32 d,a;' (register source) and 'mov.f32 k,0.1;' (immediate source), grounding both bounded base source categories for the scalar mov form; no .b32 scalar register/immediate example was read (GAP-4).
Section 9.2 states that for some instructions the destination operand is optional and a bit bucket operand denoted with an underscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register.
.b32 is a fundamental type specifier of basic type 'Bits (untyped)'; Table 8 lists .b8, .b16, .b32, .b64, .b128 under 'Bits (untyped)'.

A fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size; register variables are always of a fundamental type, and instructions operate on these types; the same type-size specifiers are used for variable definitions and instruction typing.

Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations; aside from 1-bit predicate registers, scalar registers have a width of 8-, 16-, 32-, 64-, or 128-bits (32-bit width is therefore possible for .b32 registers); registers are not fully addressable.

Type compatibility: operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility; two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size.

mov Notes state that 'Although only predicate and bit-size types are required, we include the arithmetic types for the programmer's convenience'; bit-size types such as .b32 are among the types required by mov. The kernel/function type restriction (.u32/.u64 only) concerns the out-of-scope fname/kernel forms.

The instruction type .b32 is the 'Bits (untyped)' fundamental type of width 32 bits; operands d and a are typed .b32 or a type compatible with .b32 (any 32-bit fundamental type under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rule; exact formulation open, OQ-7).
The scalar mov syntax has no modifier position; the bounded base mov.b32 form has no modifiers (no .sat or other modifier exists in the mov syntax block).
Static precondition PRE-1: the instruction type specifier .b32 is a valid bit-size fundamental type of 32-bit width.
Static precondition PRE-2: operands d and a are type-compatible with instruction type .b32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules.
Static precondition PRE-3: the destination operand d denotes a declared register variable in the .reg state space (or the bit bucket '_', applicability open question PTX-MOV-SEM2-047).
Static precondition PRE-4: the source operand a is a register variable or an immediate value.
Static precondition PRE-5: if a guard is present, it is a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
Static precondition PRE-6: base mov (and therefore the bounded base mov.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for mov.b32 (for example, no requirement on source operand values, and no flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted.

State read: the instruction reads source operand a. When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when a is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.

State read: when a guard is present, the value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. The general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 executes for threads whose guard predicate is True (PTX-9.3-MOV-035).

State write: when the instruction executes with a real destination register, the destination register d is updated with the value of source operand a. The source states no other register write for the bounded base mov.b32 form.

State write locality: only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed; no memory state space, special-register state space, carry flag, status register, or condition-code component is written by the bounded base mov.b32 (the base form has no such operands).

Guard-false state effect: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the represented consequence is that the instruction does not execute and no state component changes. This consequence is now source-resolved: section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @) explicitly states 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035) and its Semantics line is 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036); combined with the general rules that all PTX instructions may be predicated (PTX-9.3-MOV-016) and that all instructions have an optional guard predicate prefix @{!}p (PTX-9.3-MOV-021), the clause applies to the bounded base mov.b32. Formerly ASSUMPTION PTX-MOV-SEM1-034 in semantics-v1; reclassified after the v2 source-bundle supplement resolved bundle GAP-1. The official do-nothing clause itself is SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-072.
The mov Semantics block contains, verbatim, 'd = a;' as its first line, followed by 'd = sreg;', 'd = &avar;', and 'd = &avar+imm;'. For the bounded base unit, only 'd = a;' is in scope.

Copy semantics: the value written to the destination register d equals the value of source operand a (a bit-for-bit copy of the 32-bit untyped .b32 value). This is derived from 'Write register d with the value of a.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-004), the Semantics line 'd = a;' (PTX-9.3-MOV-006), and the .b32 'Bits (untyped)' 32-bit type (PTX-9.3-MOV-024, PTX-9.3-MOV-026). No arithmetic, conversion, or truncation is involved.

Guard-true behavior: when the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction value of source operand a is read, and the destination register d is updated with that value. This is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036).

Guard-false behavior: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged. Same source-resolved consequence as PTX-MOV-SEM2-034, stated at the behavior level; reclassified from ASSUMPTION (PTX-MOV-SEM1-038) to DERIVED_INTERPRETATION after the v2 supplement provided the explicit official clause (PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036).

Determinism: the execution relation for mov.b32 is deterministic for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction, because the value written is fully determined by the value read (a pure copy, no arithmetic) and the guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (bundle GAP-2; architecture assumption A-3); this is a derived interpretation stated as proof obligation PRF-1.

No scalar mov.b32 register/immediate value-copy example was found in the evidence read (bundle GAP-4). The canonical mov.b32 example 'mov.b32 r1, %tid.x;' (PTX-9.3-MOV-030) uses a special-register source, which is out of the bounded base scope. The scalar base form is grounded by the syntax type list, the description, and the Semantics line 'd = a;' only.

No explicit error, trap, or undefined-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 17 NOT_FOUND; GAP-3). The absence is not asserted as a positive source fact; no error or undefined behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is unresolved.
No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made.

Execution-result representation design (architecture D-8): an instruction-local outcome has at least two cases, executed (with updated destination) and guard-false (no state change, per derived interpretation PTX-MOV-SEM2-034); no error constructor is proposed because no explicit exceptional behavior for the bounded base mov.b32 is evidenced (GAP-3).

PTX ISA Notes for scalar mov: 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.'; taking the address of kernel entry functions requires PTX ISA version 3.1 or later (the kernel-address note concerns the out-of-scope kernel form).

Target ISA Notes for scalar mov: 'mov.f64 requires sm_13 or higher.' and 'Taking the address of kernel entry functions requires sm_35 or higher.'; no family-specific target restriction is stated for the scalar mov.b32 register/immediate value-copy form in the scalar section read.

The scalar base mov.b32 form's target set is not directly evidenced: 'Supported on all target architectures.' was read in the vector section 9.7.9.4 (PTX-9.3-MOV-013) and in the general @ predication section 9.7.13.2 (PTX-9.3-MOV-036); both concern forms other than the scalar mov.b32 value-copy base form, so neither establishes the scalar base form's target set without further evidence (bundle GAP-7; architecture assumption A-8).

Whether the bit bucket '_' is a permitted destination for the scalar mov.b32 value-copy form is not explicitly evidenced in the scalar section; only the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-9.3-MOV-019) and the vector-form sink usage (PTX-9.3-MOV-012) were found (bundle GAP-6; architecture AMB-3/OQ-2).

The allowed range and encoding for constant immediate source operands of mov are not stated in the evidence; only the description 'register variable or an immediate value' and the example 'mov.f32 k,0.1;' were found (bundle GAP-5; architecture OQ-8).

Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations, differ from other state spaces in that they are not fully addressable; scalar registers have widths of 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128 bits; and register variables are subject to the official register-section notes on spilling, ABI function-scope restriction, and legacy module-scope handling.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: The spilling, function-scope/ABI, and legacy module-scope notes are compilation-level notes recorded in the official register section; they are not modeled in the instruction-local semantics (see PTX-MOV-SEM2-065). Interpretive tail separated from the SOURCE_FACT statement per semantic-critic v1 finding F-1.

semantic_claims.statement: Variable declaration rules: all storage for data is specified with variable declarations; a declaration names the state space, type and size, name, optional array size, optional initializer, and optional fixed address; predicate variables may only be declared in the register state space.
Parameterized variable names are supported: e.g., '.reg .b32 %r<100>;' declares %r0..%r99; the shorthand may be used with any fundamental type and any state space.

Section 9.7.9.4 defines a distinct vector pack/unpack mov form (HTML anchor data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-mov-2, lines 15075-15152) whose type set also includes .b32; its description, notes, and examples concern pack/unpack behavior and are out of the bounded base scope (AMB-1).

The special register (.sreg) state space holds predefined, platform-specific registers such as grid, cluster, CTA, and thread parameters, clock counters, and performance monitoring registers; all special registers are predefined.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: This is the state space behind the out-of-scope sreg source category (PTX-MOV-SEM2-063); the sreg source category is out of the bounded base scope (PTX-MOV-SEM2-013). Interpretive tail separated from the SOURCE_FACT statement per semantic-critic v1 finding F-1.

semantic_claims.statement: For variables in .const, .global, .local, and .shared state spaces, mov places the non-generic address of the variable into the destination register; the generic address may be produced by first taking the in-space address with mov and converting with cvta, or directly with cvta.
semantic_claims.interpretation_note: This address semantics concerns the out-of-scope avar/avar+imm forms; the device-function-parameter copy-on-stack note also concerns an out-of-scope form (PTX-MOV-SEM2-063). Interpretive tail separated from the SOURCE_FACT statement per semantic-critic v1 finding F-1.

semantic_claims.statement: Official example in section 4.3: 'mov.b32 r1, %tid.x;' with '.reg .b32 r1, r2;' declarations; %tid.x is a special register, so this example uses the out-of-scope sreg source category (relevant to GAP-4).

Section 5.2.2 restricts .u8, .s8, and .b8 instruction types to ld, st, add, sub, min, max, neg, and cvt; .b32 is not in the restricted list, and no .b32-specific restriction for mov was found in the sections read (negative evidence).
st.param and ld.param instructions used for argument passing cannot be predicated; the exception does not mention mov, so the general predication applicability to mov is not contradicted.

Minimal machine state design (architecture D-5, D-14): the state for the bounded base mov.b32 is the pair (value-register file, predicate-register file); no memory, shared, special-register, or concurrency state is required by the base form's syntax and description.

Instruction representation design (architecture D-1, D-16): a mov.b32 instruction is represented as an optional guard (@{!}p), mnemonic mov, type specifier .b32, no modifier, destination operand d, and a single source operand a in that order.

Value domain design (architecture D-11, D-3): the value domain for .b32 is proposed as a fixed-width 32-bit untyped bit-value domain, because .b32 is the 'Bits (untyped)' basic type and mov Notes state bit-size types are required by mov.

Execution-semantics representation design (architecture D-25): the future execution semantics for mov.b32 is designed to be represented as an execution relation between (state, instruction) and state, not merely as a function, so that determinism and frame/locality obligations are non-vacuous.

Aliasing/read-before-write: because the semantics is a value copy (d = a;), the value of a is read before the destination update; if d and a denote the same register, the register retains its own value. No official scalar mov example with d == a was read (related to GAP-4); this derived interpretation holds at the strength of the copy rule.

OQ-1: which future units will model the sreg, avar/avar+imm, fname, and kernel source categories of section 9.7.9.3, and what shared foundations (special-register state space PTX-9.3-MOV-027; address semantics PTX-9.3-MOV-005; function/kernel-address semantics PTX-9.3-MOV-007/008/009) will they require; these are out of the bounded base scope.

OQ-4: whether the vector pack/unpack mov.b32 form of section 9.7.9.4 (PTX-9.3-MOV-011..014) should be modeled as a separate later unit; the bounded task covers only the scalar value-copy form (AMB-1).

OQ-6: whether compilation-level register notes (spilling, function-scope/ABI restriction, legacy module-scope handling; PTX-9.3-MOV-026) impose constraints that a future program-level semantics must model; they are excluded from the instruction-local architecture.

OQ-7: how the bit-size compatibility rule ('The bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size', PTX-9.3-MOV-025) should be formulated for mov.b32 operand typing: whether a register declared .u32, .s32, or .f32 is an acceptable operand for instruction type .b32, and how immediate values are typed under the same rule.

OQ-8: whether an immediate source for mov.b32 is a 32-bit constant literal and how immediate constants are typed and validated against the instruction type (PTX-9.3-MOV-010, PTX-9.3-MOV-025); the allowed range and encoding are not stated (GAP-5).

OQ-9: the exact Lean statement of the copy-fidelity candidate obligation PRF-7 ('the value written equals the value read', grounded in PTX-9.3-MOV-006 'd = a;') is a semantic-phase matter; the architecture records the candidate family only.
OQ-5: the exact Lean encoding of the 1-bit predicate register value domain (PTX-9.3-MOV-026 states predicate registers are 1-bit) is a Lean-mapping decision for a later phase.

Section 9.7.13 'Control Flow Instructions' is the general control-flow section of PTX ISA 9.3: 'The following PTX instructions and syntax are for controlling execution in a PTX program: {} @ bra call ret exit' (HTML lines 21788-21800; PDF page 399). The @ construct is listed among the control-flow constructs; section 9.7.13.2 defines the general predication form.

Section 9.7.13.1 'Control Flow Instructions: {}' defines instruction grouping: '{ instructionList }' creates a group of instructions used primarily for defining a function body, and also provides a mechanism for determining variable scope. Its example uses mov inside a braced group: '{ add.s32 a,b,c; mov.s32 d,a; }'. This establishes the 'instruction or instruction block' notion referenced by the general predication clause of section 9.7.13.2 (HTML lines 21801-21824; PDF page 399).

Section 9.7.13.2 'Control Flow Instructions: @' explicitly defines the false-guard state effect for the general predication form: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (HTML lines 21826-21839; PDF page 400). This is the explicit official false-guard no-op clause requested by the Gate B rejection; by the general predicability rule it is the applicable evidence for predicated instructions including mov.b32.

Section 9.7.13.2 Semantics line: 'If {!}p then instruction', i.e. the instruction executes exactly when the (possibly negated) guard predicate holds. PTX ISA Notes for the general @ form: 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.'; Target ISA Notes for the general @ form: 'Supported on all target architectures.' (HTML lines 21840-21845; PDF page 400). The target note concerns the general predication form, not the scalar mov.b32 value-copy target set (see PTX-MOV-SEM2-046).

Section 9.7.13.2 Examples use the general guard forms: '@!p div.f32 ratio,x,y // avoid division by zero' (negated guard guarding an instruction) and '@q bra L23; // conditional branch' (positive guard guarding a branch) (HTML lines 21846-21853; PDF page 400). These illustrate the general guard syntax that applies to predicated instructions.

Section 9.7.13.3 'Control Flow Instructions: bra' records bra-specific guard behavior as 'if (p) { pc = tgt; }' — the guard-true effect is performed only when the predicate holds. This is bra-specific neighboring control-flow context; it is not asserted to govern mov.b32 directly. mov.b32 guard behavior is governed by the general @ predication clause (PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036; PTX-MOV-SEM2-072/073) (HTML lines 21859-21876; PDF page 401).

Derivation chain for mov.b32 guard behavior: (1) 'All PTX instructions may be predicated' (PTX-9.3-MOV-016); (2) 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate ... prefix an instruction with @{!}p' (PTX-9.3-MOV-021); (3) the general predication form's explicit rule 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' and its Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036); therefore the bounded base mov.b32, when predicated, executes iff the complete guard expression is true, and does nothing (no state change) when the complete guard expression is false. This derived consequence consolidates the chain behind PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038.

resolved_open_questions.summary: OQ-2/OQ-3 (semantics-v1): the guard-false 'no state update' interpretation needed human approval and would require a source-curation supplement if explicit official evidence were required. RESOLVED in semantics-v2: the v2 source-bundle supplement provided the explicit official clause of section 9.7.13.2 (PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036); the mov.b32 guard-false consequence is now DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038) and is no longer presented as a human assumption.

future_theorem_obligation_topics.description: Determinism of the execution relation for mov.b32: at most one resulting state for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction. Derived interpretation PTX-MOV-SEM2-039 (determinism not explicitly stated, GAP-2); no arithmetic-result assumption is needed because mov performs no arithmetic.

Destination-only update / frame: when mov.b32 executes with a register destination, only the destination register may change; every other value register and predicate register is unchanged. Grounded in PTX-MOV-SEM2-032/033.

Bit-bucket discard: when the destination is '_', execution changes no value register. Depends on the general-rule-supported bit-bucket interpretation (AMB-3; PTX-MOV-SEM2-047); scalar mov.b32-specific demonstration remains an open question, which is non-blocking for the base register-destination semantics.

Guard-false frame: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the entire state is unchanged. UNBLOCKED in semantics-v2: grounded in DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038 (source-resolved via section 9.7.13.2 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036); the previous block (human approval of the guard-false assumption) is lifted because the consequence is now an evidence-backed derived interpretation; it remains subject to the ordinary Gate B review of this semantics.

Guard-behavior: the instruction executes if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true, covering no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly. Grounded in PTX-MOV-SEM2-009/037 and guard_semantics, now also the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-9.3-MOV-036).

Result-domain membership: when mov.b32 executes, the value written to the destination lies in the 32-bit bit-size value domain of .b32. DISPOSITION RECORDED (semantic-critic v1 finding F-3): per architecture-critic v1 F-3 and semantics-critic v1 F-3, PRF-6 is reclassified as a definitional/validation-style well-formedness obligation (VAL-style, like VAL-1/VAL-2) rather than a semantic proof obligation, because under the typed register-file representation it would otherwise be vacuous; the final adoption of this disposition is confirmed at the theorem-design stage (Gate C / theorem-strength gate).

Copy fidelity (candidate): when the instruction executes with a register source, the value written to the destination equals the value read from the source ('d = a;', PTX-9.3-MOV-006). Meaningful semantic property for a value-copy instruction; the exact formal statement is a semantic-phase matter (OQ-9; PTX-MOV-SEM2-068).
